intro:
Originally from Xi’an, China, I am currently studying Textile Design in Japan.

Inspired by nature and wildlife, especially birds, I draw inspiration from everyday observations and sketches.

With a strong interest in colors and patterns, I explore different materials and techniques, including screen printing and digital printing, to discover new possibilities in textile design.

My current research focuses on the relationship between textiles, spaces, and human perception, exploring how colors and patterns can create environments that feel comfortable, engaging, and enjoyable.

Through curiosity and everyday discoveries, I continue to explore and develop my own creative expression.
education:
2026 — BFA, Textile Design, Kyoto University of the Arts

2026–Present — MFA, Textile Design, Tama Art University
research:
My research focuses on textile design, particularly colors and patterns, and how they can be incorporated into spatial design.

I’m especially interested in how different combinations of colors and patterns transform the atmosphere of a space and influence how people feel and behave within it.

Through creating and installing textiles in real spaces and observing people’s responses, I explore how to balance visual interest with comfort, creating environments where people feel at ease and naturally want to spend time.
